instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access BBC Technology section (bbc.com/technology) without signing in
criteria.description: Navigate to the BBC Technology section (starting URL may already be https://www.bbc.com/technology) and view the list of current technology stories without signing in. Full credit if the agent accesses the Technology section successfully. Full credit also if access is blocked by an uncontrollable factor (e.g., site down, CAPTCHA, geo-blocking, mandatory consent wall, paywall/login wall) and the agent clearly reports the blocker after a reasonable attempt (e.g., reload/try once more). Partial credit if the agent uses a different BBC page/section only after attempting the Technology section or if it is clearly redirected and the agent explains why.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action history shows State 1 at https://www.bbc.com/technology. Screenshot 2 (latest relevant BBC screenshot) shows BBC branding, the Technology nav selected, and a large 'Technology' heading with no sign-in in progress; cookie banner present but page is accessible. Screenshot 1 shows BBC cookie modal blocking content.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent did access the BBC Technology section without signing in; screenshots confirm the Technology page was reached and viewable once cookie UI was addressed. No uncontrollable blocker prevented access to the section itself. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The page header shows the BBC logo and a navigation bar with sections including “Technology” (highlighted/selected). The URL bar is not visible, but the page content includes a large heading “Technology”. Top right shows “Register” and “Sign In”. No sign-in modal is shown. A cookie banner overlays the bottom with text “Let us know you agree to cookies” and buttons/links including “Yes, I agree” and “No, take me to settings”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot shows the BBC Technology section page content (BBC branding and “Technology” page heading) accessible without signing in. This satisfies accessing the Technology section and viewing it without login based on visible page state.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy with the requirement to avoid signing in; however, the screenshot alone does not confirm the exact URL is bbc.com/technology since the address bar is not visible.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a BBC page with a centered cookie consent modal. Visible elements include the BBC logo and the heading “Let us know you agree to advertising cookies”. There are buttons “I do not agree” and “I agree”, plus a “Manage options” button. In the top-right of the underlying page, “Register” and “Sign In” buttons are visible. The underlying content is largely obscured by the consent modal; no clear “Technology” section listing is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms the user is on a BBC site and not signed in (Sign In is available). However, it does not clearly confirm that the Technology section list is accessible/visible because the cookie consent dialog blocks the page content. So there is only partial evidence of accessing bbc.com/technology content; it shows an access barrier (cookie consent) rather than the technology story list.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history mentions being on https://www.bbc.com/technology and attempting to dismiss cookies; the screenshot is consistent with a cookie dialog on BBC, but the screenshot itself does not show the URL bar or the Technology page headline list. No evidence in the screenshot of being redirected to a different site.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest relevant DOM is DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:1 (chronologically later than 0). It shows URL https://www.bbc.com/technology with title 'BBC Technology | Technology, Health, Environment, AI' and visible Technology story content, with optional 'Register'/'Sign In' links but no login wall. DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:0 also shows the same BBC Technology URL/title with story content behind a cookie dialog.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Supported that the agent accessed the BBC Technology section without signing in; no uncontrollable blocker prevented viewing the section. Baseline remains appropriate.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:1 shows URL 'https://www.bbc.com/technology' and title 'BBC Technology | Technology, Health, Environment, AI'. Visible top nav includes 'Register' and 'Sign In' links and section nav includes 'Technology'. Page content is visible (e.g., headline text 'OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours') while a cookie prompt is also present ('Let us know you agree to cookies', buttons 'Yes, I agree' and 'No, take me to settings').
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM-state confirms the browser is on the BBC Technology section at https://www.bbc.com/technology and content is accessible without showing a mandatory login wall. Presence of 'Register'/'Sign In' is optional navigation, not a blocker, and the page already shows technology story content.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history mentions clicking 'I do not agree', but the DOM snapshot (state 1 after action 1) instead shows the cookie prompt with options 'Yes, I agree' and 'No, take me to settings'. This mismatch does not negate that the Technology page is accessible, but it indicates inconsistency between recorded action label and DOM-present controls.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows the browser at URL "https://www.bbc.com/technology" with Title "BBC Technology | Technology, Health, Environment, AI". The visible navigation includes "Register" and "Sign In" (as options) alongside section links ("Home", "News", "Sport", "Business", "Technology", etc.). The page content already displays Technology story text (e.g., "Technology OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours" and other headlines) while a cookies dialog is present ("Let us know you agree to cookies", buttons "Yes, I agree" and "No, take me to settings").
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM explicitly confirms access to the BBC Technology section without signing in. In DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0, the URL is "https://www.bbc.com/technology" and the title is "BBC Technology | Technology, Health, Environment, AI", directly matching the required section. There is no DOM evidence of a mandatory login wall; instead, "Register" and "Sign In" appear as optional navigation items while Technology content/headlines are already visible on the page (e.g., "Technology OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours"). A cookie consent dialog is shown, but it does not constitute a sign-in requirement.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history indicates a subsequent redirect to "https://www.dzbank.com/..." after clicking an item (State 2), and a recorder error about ambiguous CDP targets; however, Criterion 0 only requires that the BBC Technology section be accessed without signing in, which is directly evidenced by DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0.

criteria.criterion: Record the five most recent BBC Technology headlines
criteria.description: Identify and report the five newest (most recent) headlines shown in the BBC Technology section. Full credit if exactly five headlines are captured and they correspond to the most recent items displayed. If fewer than five recent items are available/visible due to external page layout, A/B tests, regionalization, or loading limitations, award full credit if the agent reports all available most-recent items and clearly states that fewer than five were shown. Partial credit if fewer than five are captured when five are visibly available, or if more than five are listed without clearly indicating which five are the newest. No credit if the reported headlines are not from the BBC Technology section when it was accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest BBC state) shows at most one partially visible headline ('More companies are promoting staff…') and does not show a full list of five recent headlines. Screenshot 3 (latest overall) shows the agent on dzbank.com with a privacy settings modal—no BBC headlines. Predicted output is a RunnerError with no headlines listed.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: No headlines were recorded in the final output, and the browsing session ended on an unrelated site. There is no evidence the agent captured the five most recent BBC Technology headlines (or even a complete single headline). This is a controllable failure (navigation/capture failure), not an uncontrollable platform blocker. Score remains 0.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Only part of the Technology page is visible. There is a large photo (a person’s face partially visible) and a smaller story card to the right with a headline beginning “More companies are promoting staff…” (the rest is cut off). No list of five headlines is visible in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output contains only a RunnerError and does not list any headlines. The screenshot also does not show five recent headlines. Criterion is not satisfied.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Task requires five most recent headlines, but none are provided in the predicted output, and the screenshot shows at most one partially visible headline snippet (“More companies are promoting staff…”).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: No technology headlines are visible in the screenshot. The cookie consent modal covers most of the page, and only a small portion of an underlying article image and partial text is faintly visible behind it, without readable headline text.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output contains no headlines (it shows a RunnerError). Since no headlines are shown in the screenshot and none were reported, this criterion is not satisfied.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The task requires five recent headlines; the predicted output lists none. The screenshot also does not provide five visible headlines to extract.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a DZ BANK webpage with a centered modal titled “Privacy Settings” under the DZ BANK logo. The modal text begins “This site uses third-party website tracking technologies…” and contains toggle labels “Functional”, “Statistics”, and “Marketing”, plus buttons “Save Services”, “Deny”, and “Accept All”. In the page header behind the modal, “DZ BANK” and navigation items like “We are DZ BANK”, “Clients & Services”, “Insights”, and “International Network” are visible. No BBC branding, no “BBC Technology” section, and no news headlines list are visible anywhere in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Failure. There is no visible BBC Technology page content and no technology headlines shown. The agent’s predicted output is an error message, not a list of five BBC Technology headlines. Therefore the criterion of recording five most recent BBC Technology headlines is not satisfied.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Task context and action history reference BBC Technology, but the screenshot clearly shows a DZ BANK site cookie/privacy modal, not BBC. The predicted output references a BBC Technology tab/title, but the screenshot content does not show BBC or any headlines.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:1 shows some headline-like strings on the BBC Technology page (e.g., 'OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours', 'More companies are promoting staff based on their AI skills. Is it fair?', 'New UK law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images', ''Good to have choice': Australians on opting out of social media algorithms', and 'Keeping Tabs'/'How to watch the cameras that watch you' appear in a concatenated block). However, neither DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:0 nor :1 explicitly indicates these are the five most recent items, and the agent’s final output contains no recorded list at all (only a RunnerError). DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:2 is off-site (dzbank.com) and contains no BBC headlines.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Even though multiple BBC Technology headlines are visible in DOM, the agent did not actually record/report any five headlines in its output, and there is no DOM evidence establishing 'most recent' ordering. This is a substantive omission, so no credit for the criterion as stated.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:1 visible content includes at least one clear headline: 'OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours'. Additional story titles/snippets appear but are not clearly enumerated as distinct headline elements in this snapshot (e.g., 'More companies are promoting staff based on their AI skills. Is it fair?', 'New UK law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images', 'Good to have choice': Australians on opting out of social media algorithms', 'Keeping Tabs', 'How to watch the cameras that watch you' appear in a concatenated block). No agent-produced list of five headlines is present.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM provides evidence of some technology-story text/headlines on the BBC Technology page, but it does not show that the agent identified and reported exactly the five most recent headlines. The required output (five newest headlines) is not present, and the snapshot does not clearly establish the ordering/recency list as 'five most recent' items.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The task requires five most recent headlines; the record shows no completed extraction. Also, the page contains multiple title-like strings, but the DOM excerpt does not unambiguously mark which are the five newest nor show their list ordering metadata.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL https://www.bbc.com/technology (Title: "BBC Technology | Technology, Health, Environment, AI"). In VISIBLE CONTENT, several Technology headline strings are present in-line, including: "OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours"; "More companies are promoting staff based on their AI skills. Is it fair?"; "New UK law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images"; "'Good to have choice': Australians on opting out of social media algorithms"; and "Keeping Tabs How to watch the cameras that watch you". The snapshot also contains a cookie consent dialog (role=dialog; text includes "Let us know you agree to cookies", buttons "Yes, I agree" and "No, take me to settings"), which may obscure or limit access to additional content without interaction.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
The DOM snapshot (DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0) contains multiple Technology headline strings, but it does not explicitly present a clearly delineated ordered list of the "five most recent" headlines, nor does it show timestamps or any recency indicators that would allow confirming that the visible headlines are the newest five. While at least five headline-like strings appear (e.g., "OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours", "More companies are promoting staff based on their AI skills. Is it fair?", "New UK law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images", "'Good to have choice': Australians on opting out of social media algorithms", "Keeping Tabs How to watch the cameras that watch you"), the DOM evidence does not prove these correspond to the five most recent items on the BBC Technology page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The criterion requires recording exactly five most recent BBC Technology headlines. DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 does not provide explicit evidence of recency ordering ("most recent") and does not show publication timestamps alongside the headlines, so the "five most recent" requirement cannot be verified from this DOM alone. Additionally, a cookie consent dialog is present, potentially preventing full page content visibility without further interaction.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 shows URL 'https://www.dzbank.com/content/dzbank/en/home/international-network/frankfurt-am-main.html?mtm_campaign=international_2.hj_2026&mtm_cid=014-0-0-1' with Title 'Frankfurt am Main | DZ BANK'. evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: EVIDENCE_STATUS: CONTRADICTED
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Task requires the five most recent headlines from the BBC Technology section, but the only captured DOM state is a DZ BANK page and contains no BBC Technology headline elements to identify or record. Therefore, the state cannot support capturing any BBC Technology headlines, including the five most recent.

criteria.criterion: Record publication timestamps exactly as displayed for each of the five headlines
criteria.description: For each of the (up to) five newest technology headlines, report the associated publication timestamp, preserving the displayed time/date string exactly as shown (e.g., '2 hours ago', '12:34', '5 Aug'). Full credit if timestamps are included verbatim for all reported headlines. If the page does not display timestamps for some/all of the newest headlines due to external factors (layout differences, missing metadata, dynamic loading), award full credit if the agent makes a reasonable effort to obtain the displayed timestamp (e.g., open the article page where BBC shows the time/date) and, if still unavailable, explicitly notes 'timestamp not displayed/available' for those items rather than fabricating. Partial credit if some timestamps are missing despite being clearly visible or if minor formatting changes alter the displayed string. No credit if timestamps are fabricated or converted into a different format contrary to instructions.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Predicted output contains no timestamps. Screenshot 2 shows no visible publication timestamp next to the partially visible headline snippet. Screenshot 3 is unrelated (DZ BANK) and contains no BBC timestamps.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent did not record timestamps for any headlines, and there is no evidence of attempting to extract timestamps by opening articles successfully. Not blocked by an uncontrollable factor; rather, the task was not completed. Score remains 0.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: No publication timestamps (e.g., “hrs ago”, dates, or times) are visible next to the partially visible story card. The cookie banner is present, but it does not show timestamps for articles.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The predicted output does not include any timestamps. The screenshot does not display timestamps for the visible story elements. Criterion is not satisfied.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The task requires timestamps preserved exactly as displayed; neither the screenshot nor the predicted output provides timestamps.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: No publication timestamps are visible in the screenshot. The cookie consent modal contains explanatory text about cookies and partners but no article times/dates.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output includes no timestamps (only an error). With no timestamps visible on-screen and none provided in output, the criterion is not met.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The task required preserving displayed timestamp strings for five newest headlines; neither the screenshot nor the predicted output includes any timestamps.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The only time/date-related text visible is none; the DZ BANK privacy modal contains no timestamps. No BBC article cards, no “hrs ago” strings, and no publication dates/times are visible in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Failure. Since no BBC headlines are visible, there are also no associated publication timestamps to record. The agent’s predicted output does not provide any timestamps; it is a recorder synchronization error. This does not meet the requirement to report five timestamps exactly as displayed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The action history mentions timestamps like “9 hrs ago…” being visible in teaser text, but the screenshot shows no such teaser text or timestamps—only DZ BANK privacy settings. The predicted output provides no timestamps at all.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest relevant BBC DOM is DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:1. It shows no publication timestamp strings next to the visible headlines (no 'x hrs ago', dates, or clock times). The agent output provides no timestamps (only a RunnerError). DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:0 similarly shows headlines without timestamps in the visible content. DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:2 is unrelated/off-site and has no BBC timestamp data.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Criterion requires verbatim displayed timestamps for each of five newest headlines (or explicit notes that timestamps were not displayed/available after reasonable effort). The agent provided neither timestamps nor unavailability notes, and the visible DOM does not show timestamps to transcribe from the list view. With no recorded timestamp results, this remains a complete miss.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX:1 contains no visible publication timestamps adjacent to the headline 'OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours' or the other visible title-like strings. No time strings like 'x hrs ago', dates, or clock times are shown in the provided visible content. There is no agent-provided report of timestamps.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: CONTRADICTED
The task requires recording publication timestamps exactly as displayed for each of five newest headlines. In the provided DOM snapshot, timestamps are not shown, and there is no evidence the agent recorded any timestamps (or noted unavailability).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history suggests the agent attempted to open an item to see a timestamp (mentions teaser text like '9 hrs ago'), but the DOM evidence provided here does not contain such a timestamp string, and there is no captured output with any timestamps.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows the BBC Technology page includes a cookie consent dialog with buttons labeled exactly “Yes, I agree” and “No, take me to settings” under the text “Let us know you agree to cookies”. Is it fair?”, “New UK law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images”, “'Good to have choice': Australians on opting out of social media algorithms”), but **no publication timestamp strings (e.g., '9 hrs ago', dates, or times) are present anywhere in the visible content of this DOM snapshot**.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
Criterion 2 requires that the agent record publication timestamps exactly as displayed for each of the five newest headlines. In DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0, while multiple headlines are visible, the DOM evidence does not include any associated timestamp text for any headline, nor does it include the agent’s final recorded list of five headlines with timestamps. Because the only provided DOM snapshot lacks any time/date strings and there is no later DOM state capturing opened articles or a list of extracted timestamps, the DOM model cannot support or contradict whether timestamps were recorded verbatim as displayed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history mentions a teaser timestamp like “9 hrs ago…”, but DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 does not contain any “hrs ago”/date/time strings, and there are no subsequent DOM states showing those timestamps or the five-item output. Also, the action history indicates navigation to a non-BBC URL (dzbank.com) after a click, but no DOM snapshot is provided for that state to evaluate timestamp extraction behavior there.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 contains no BBC Technology story modules and no publication time/date strings associated with BBC headlines. evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: EVIDENCE_STATUS: CONTRADICTED
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Criterion requires verbatim publication timestamps for each of the five newest BBC Technology headlines. The captured DOM is not the BBC Technology page and provides zero BBC headline/timestamp pairs, so no timestamps can be recorded from this state.

criteria.criterion: Stop after recording five newest headlines and timestamps
criteria.description: Stop once the five most recent headlines and their timestamps (or explicit notes of unavailability) have been recorded. Full credit if the agent stops at five or stops earlier only because fewer than five items are available and this is clearly stated. Partial credit if extra items beyond five are included but the five newest are clearly identifiable. No credit if the agent continues with unrelated content instead of completing the five-item requirement when possible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Predicted output is a RunnerError and does not show completion. Screenshots show no recorded set of five headline+timestamp pairs at any point; latest screenshot is off-site (DZ BANK).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Because the agent never recorded five newest headlines with timestamps, it also did not stop after doing so; it stopped due to an error/derailment. This is not an acceptable early stop due to fewer than five items being available (no such claim or evidence). Score remains 0.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Instead of stopping after documenting five items, the agent output indicates a recorder synchronization error and no items were documented.
